said: The Berliner Zeitung reported on 7 May 2023 (dpa) that a March 2023 statement by Nigeria's president made the Oba of Benin owner of the returned Benin bronzes, so that loans now need his approval, and that Swiss ethnologist Brigitta Hauser-Schäublin called the ownership agreement poorly worded for turning public property into private property while jurist Matthias Goldmann said the Oba's claim was foreseeable. IBTimes reported on 10 June 2023 that Saxony paused further returns and that Nigerian art historian Peju Layiwola called the Western reaction an excuse not to return the artefacts. Hermann Parzinger, whose foundation runs the Humboldt Forum's Ethnological Museum, said about a third of the works would stay on show in the Humboldt Forum as a long-term loan and that returns came without conditions.
response: Parzinger said he did not believe the Oba declaration put future returns in doubt; culture minister Claudia Roth said she was surprised and irritated by the reaction and that Nigeria as owner should decide (IBTimes, 10 June 2023); the Foreign Office said the return was unconditional (Berliner Zeitung, 7 May 2023).

headline: Freelance guide says she was dropped for calling the West Bank 'apartheid'
said: The New Arab reported on 4 December 2023 that the Jewish Museum Berlin ended the engagement of freelance guide Udi Raz on 25 October 2023 after she described Israel as an apartheid state on tours, citing Amnesty International, and that Raz believed the word was the reason. Raz told The Left Berlin on 12 November 2023 that the official reason was her use of the term and called the decision a manifestation of gaslighting. Der Freitag reported on 24 June 2024 that the museum said she had broken mandatory quality standards by repeatedly confronting groups with her personal political views.
where: The New Arab, Der Freitag, The Left Berlin
response: A museum spokesperson told The New Arab that the guide overwhelmed groups with a personal political stance that conflicted with its educational standards; press spokesperson Margret Karsch told Der Freitag she had not considered groups' prior knowledge or offered varied, academically grounded perspectives.
rule: §1 all; §3 rank 2 + rank 4; named because she put her name to it in interviews

headline: Zeughaus repair grew into a rebuild; no reopening before 2031, says the president
said: The Berliner Zeitung reported on 23 January 2026 that the DHM's Zeughaus, closed since 2021 for air-conditioning damage, will stay shut longer than previously communicated, with foundation president Raphael Gross telling rbb24 he does not expect a reopening before 2031 and calling even that a positive scenario. The paper wrote that what began as a technical repair grew into a comprehensive renovation with a second entrance, new routing and a family area, which it said sounds more like a new build, that financing for interim solutions is unresolved, and that the delay has renewed debate about overrunning construction projects in Berlin.
response: Gross said reliable reopening dates are not possible while planning is unfinished and that he is open in principle to interim displays of parts of the new permanent exhibition, funding permitting; the museum said the Pei building's 'Roads not Taken' show has been extended to 2026 (Berliner Zeitung, 23 January 2026).

headline: Concertgebouw cancels Hanukkah concert over IDF cantor, then settles for closed shows
said: JTA reported on 4 November 2025 that the Concertgebouw cancelled its annual Hanukkah concert set for 14 December after pressing for months for a programme change, saying the appearance of Shai Abramson, the Israeli army's chief cantor, conflicted with its mission of connecting people through music; the Chanukah Concert Foundation said the hall was adding to the isolation the Jewish community feels and announced legal action. DutchNews reported on 12 November 2025 that the two sides agreed Abramson would sing at two invitation-only concerts and the main concert would go ahead without him. NOS reported on 14 December 2025 that pro-Palestinian demonstrators briefly blocked two entrances and police made arrests, after a judge had allowed a small, quiet protest at a side entrance against the municipality's ban.
response: Director Simon Reinink called the decision extremely difficult, said the hall rarely makes exceptions to its artistic-freedom principle and expressed regret; the hall said the Jewish community would always be welcome (JTA, 4 November 2025).
outcome: Compromise announced 12 November 2025: the main concert on 14 December 2025 without Abramson, who was to sing at two private concerts.

headline: Extinction Rebellion keeps shutting the Rijksmuseum to force out sponsor ING
said: DutchNews reported on 7 September 2024 that about sixty Extinction Rebellion activists in yellow chained themselves across the gates of the museum underpass, closing the Rijksmuseum for the morning, with 33 arrested; the group estimates ING pays about 700,000 euros a year, under 0.6 per cent of the museum's income, and spokeswoman Josefien van Marlen said the sponsorship lets the bank hide its dirty face behind famous artworks. Artnet reported the activists said they would keep coming back. NL Times reported on 1 March 2025 that the group staged a visitor strike by reserving thousands of tickets and not showing up, leaving only a few hundred genuine visitors on a day the museum expected about 8,000.
response: A museum spokesperson said it closed for the safety of collection, staff and visitors and that any action jeopardising this is unacceptable, and confirmed ING has been a main sponsor since 2005 (Artnet); in March 2025 the museum said XR was preventing it from carrying out its public mission (NL Times). ING said activists should raise concerns with the bank directly and called the March action unacceptable.
outcome: No change to the ING sponsorship recorded.

headline: Four staff dismissed after the Pokémon show, one for taking a box of cards
said: The Art Newspaper reported on 25 January 2024, citing Het Parool, that the Van Gogh Museum dismissed four staff over alleged misconduct during its Pokémon collaboration: staff allegedly gave visitors insider tips on getting limited tickets and the limited Pikachu card, and another employee allegedly took a box of the cards. Artnet reported that the four, from operational services, had first been suspended in December 2023, that the gift shop had descended into chaos on opening day in September 2023, that merchandise sold out within 24 hours and that the museum withdrew the card in October 2023 because of crowds and resellers.
where: The Art Newspaper, Artnet, Het Parool
response: A museum spokesman told Het Parool it viewed the matter as an exceptional incident and declined further comment; it described the long-serving employee's tips to visitors as a breach of its procedures and codes of conduct (The Art Newspaper, Artnet).
outcome: Four dismissals; a relaunch of the card in selected Dutch game stores was due in February (Artnet).

headline: Director says the museum could be forced to close in a funding feud with the state
said: The Art Newspaper reported on 28 August 2025 that director Emilie Gordenker said the museum would be forced to close without extra state money for a 104 million euro renovation planned for 2028 to 2031, that it wanted the annual building subsidy raised from 8.5 to 11 million euros under a 1962 agreement, and that it had filed a legal complaint alleging the state breached that agreement. On 5 May 2026 the paper reported the court case adjourned indefinitely while the two sides are in confidential mediation, with culture minister Rianne Letschert telling parliament the talks must stay secret and Volt MP Laurens Dassen calling the museum a national asset.
response: The Ministry of Education, Culture and Science said independent research found its subsidy sufficient to cover necessary maintenance and that the museum would have to contribute itself to work beyond that (The Art Newspaper, 28 August 2025 and 5 May 2026). A museum spokesperson said mediation was making good progress.
outcome: Mediation ongoing as of May 2026; both sides aimed to finish before summer 2026.

headline: Artist asks the Stedelijk to take down his barricade after it refused a Gaza-protest loan
said: Artnet reported on 1 July 2024 that the Not Surprised Collective asked to borrow Ahmet Öğüt's Bakunin's Barricade, whose contract allows loans for protests, to shield students at pro-Gaza demonstrations, and said it was disappointed but not surprised when the museum offered copies of the embedded collection works instead of the originals, accusing it of putting heritage above protecting students and calling undisclosed replicas a lie to the public. The Art Newspaper reported on 5 November 2024 that Öğüt then called on the museum to remove the work from display.
response: The museum said it condemned violence against students but could not lend originals because of its duty to preserve a collection owned by the city, cited the ICOM code of ethics, said it had met the contract's reproductions option which the applicants rejected, and said it would not remove the work without a valid reason while contract terms remained under negotiation (Artnet, July 2024; The Art Newspaper, November 2024).
outcome: Work remained on display as of November 2024.

headline: Culture Council rates De Appel positively but advises zero national funding
said: In its advice on the 2025–2028 national basic infrastructure, the Raad voor Cultuur wrote that De Appel's application met the requirements and praised its curatorial programme and governance, but after weighing it against others in the category advised no subsidy against the 450,000 euros requested, noting high financial risk in its 2022 liquidity and solvency ratios and a vague audience plan. NH Nieuws reported on 17 October 2024 that the City of Amsterdam added 3.5 million euros to its arts plan so that seven organisations, De Appel among them, would receive the full four-year subsidy the Amsterdam Fund for the Arts had recommended.
where: Raad voor Cultuur advice, NH Nieuws
response: No statement from De Appel on the 2024 advice found in the sources opened.
outcome: City of Amsterdam topped up the arts plan in October 2024 so De Appel received its full municipal subsidy for 2025–2028.
